title: Armada workflow
description: An ordered set of steps, which skill runs each one, and what verdict advances it. PLAN.md §14.4 and §14.6. This file is the authoritative statement of the workflow contract; anything mirroring it is a mirror.

description.description: One line. Shown by `armada guild edit` and used when classification explains its choice.

budget.description: Ceilings for a Job running this workflow. Every field is required: a ceiling that can be omitted is a ceiling that is missing on the run where it mattered.

max_wall_clock.description: A duration such as `90m`. No bare numbers — a unitless ceiling is read wrong exactly once.

on_exhausted.description: What happens when a ceiling is reached. Exhaustion is a first-class outcome, never a silent stop (PLAN.md §14.3), which is why there is no `stop` option.

on_blocked.description: One value today. It exists as a key rather than a constant because a future workflow may want to route a block somewhere other than the human, and a key that was never there cannot be added compatibly.

id.description: Unique within the workflow. Appears in the verdict envelope as `step`.

skill.description: Which skill runs this step. Resolved against the guild's skills and the repo's (PLAN.md §14.5) — `guild verify` checks it exists, the schema cannot. Omitted when the step is satisfied by Fleet rather than by a Drone, as `review` is.

workflow.description: Run another workflow as a sub-Job: its own uuid, worktree, budget and record. The step advances on the sub-Job's verdict. Mutually exclusive with `skill`. `guild verify` resolves the name and rejects cycles.

step.description: Exactly one of `skill` (a Drone does it), `workflow` (a sub-Job does it), or neither (Fleet satisfies it, as `review` does). Two of them is ambiguous about who runs the step.

must.description: The predicate that advances this step. A verdict is only PASS if it carries evidence an external command produced (PLAN.md §14.3), so every predicate below except `always` names something that produces evidence.

scope.description: Check ids or component:check selectors, passed to `armada manifest check --scope`. Only meaningful with `check_passes`; `guild verify` resolves each against the workspace's config.

then.description: An unscoped `check_passes` would run every check in the repo, which is both slow and not what any step means.
`scope` on any other predicate is silently ignored at run time, which is how a workflow ends up gating on nothing.
